newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Bank Austria cashes in on foreign business boom.
newsitem.headline: Bank Austria cashes in on foreign business boom.

text.p: By Elizabeth Fullerton Austria's biggest bank, said on Monday parent operating profit in the first nine months rose 9.9 percent to 3.6 billion schillings ($340.3 million), boosted by strength in its businesses abroad.
"It is a satisfactory result when you look at the market and ... somewhat better than I had expected earlier in the year," chief executive Gerhard Randa told reporters.

The bank, controlled by the City of Vienna, said operating income climbed 4.7 percent to 13.3 billion schillings but noted operating costs in Austria's overcrowded banking sector remained high at 9.7 billion schillings, a 2.9 percent rise.
"I hope we can succeed in bringing down these costs a little by the year's end", Randa said.
He said he expected pressure on interest margins and earnings to continue in the fourth quarter but he declined to give more than an approximate forecast for the full year.
"We will definitely reach last year's result," was all he would say. Last year the bank posted a parent operating profit of 4.85 billion schillings.
Randa did not rule out raising the dividend from last year's 10 percent but noted: "It is better to have a reserve that you can distribute."
Shareholders' equity amounted to 45.1 billion schillings to the end of September, against 40.1 billion at the end of 1995.

Bank Austria's balance sheet reached 720.2 billion schillings at the end of September, a 6.3 percent rise on December 1995. Randa said foreign exchange activities, which reached 32.5 percent against 30.9 percent in 1995 had "developed extremely well".
Risk provisions for the full year would fall below last year's 3.41 billion schillings, the bank predicted -- a trend seen across Austria's banks.
"In total provisioning for bad debt will be lower than last year," Randa said.

The bank's chief said Bank Austria was set to merge with WestLB Austria, the Austrian unit of Germany's Westdeutsche Landesbank Girozentrale AG at the start of next year. WestLB has a 9.1 percent stake in Bank Austria
"We expect to merge WestLB Austria with Bank Austria," he said, but gave no further details.
Asked if he had his eye on any new acquisitions, Randa said: "I have no active acquisition strategy, but I am open to suggestions." ($ = 10.57 Austrian Schillings)
